## Cartesian metric (`cartesian`) {#sec-ch03-cartesian}

<!-- PROVENANCE

### Summary

On a Cartesian grid every metric quantity is a product of cell widths, and the widths are the global $\Delta x_a$ of
@sec-ch03-globalgrid, so a cell's metric does not depend on which block holds it. The cell centre is the midpoint of
its faces, which is also the volume centroid, and the non-orthogonality cosine that the cubed sphere needs
(@sec-ch03-gnomonic) is identically zero. The finite-volume operator is the plain flux divergence; there are no
geometric source terms. The type is the default when `geometry.type` is absent.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Uniform-width Cartesian metric: face areas are products of two widths, the volume the product of three,
the centre the midpoint (@eq-ch03-cartesian-metric).

**Data.** In: the block's slice of the global faces [m]. Out: widths, face areas [m$^2$], volumes [m$^3$] and
centres [m] at cells and faces, ghosts included.

**Placement.** Setup, in the coordinate's `reset`; rebuilt only when the grid is reset.

**Activation.** YAML `geometry.type: cartesian`; the default type; no couplings.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact; the face-centroid shift is identically zero.

**Evidence.** `test_coordinate`, exact; check `[C17]`; the ctest entries were not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).
:::

Local symbols: $A_{a,\pm}$ the areas of the two faces of cell $i$[^rg-741b89eeff43] normal to $x_a$
[m$^2$]; $\overline q_i$ the cell average of the generic field $q$ of appendix A, notation group 3; $\overline F_{a,\pm}$ the
face-average flux through those faces, in the units of $q$ times m s$^{-1}$.

### Derivation

For a cell $[x_{1,i-1/2}, x_{1,i+1/2}]\times[x_{2,j-1/2}, x_{2,j+1/2}]\times[x_{3,k-1/2}, x_{3,k+1/2}]$ with widths
$\Delta x_1, \Delta x_2, \Delta x_3$ the measures are the integrals of $\mathrm{d}x_2\,\mathrm{d}x_3$,
$\mathrm{d}x_1\,\mathrm{d}x_3$, $\mathrm{d}x_1\,\mathrm{d}x_2$ and $\mathrm{d}V$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_{i\pm1/2} &= \Delta x_2\,\Delta x_3, \\
A_{j\pm1/2} &= \Delta x_1\,\Delta x_3, \\
A_{k\pm1/2} &= \Delta x_1\,\Delta x_2, \\
V_i &= \Delta x_1\,\Delta x_2\,\Delta x_3.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-cartesian-metric}

The face areas of @eq-ch03-cartesian-metric are `face_area1` to `face_area3` and the volume is `cell_volume`
({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::cell_volume >}}, {{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::face_area1 >}}, {{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::face_area2 >}}, {{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::face_area3 >}}). The centroid of a uniform weight over an interval is its midpoint,
$x_{1,i} = \tfrac12(x_{1,i-1/2}+x_{1,i+1/2})$, computed in `reset` for `x1v` ({{< code src/coord/cartesian.cpp CartesianImpl::reset >}}).
Let $q$ be a conserved density (mass, momentum or energy per unit volume) and $\mathbf F$ its flux, in the units of
$q$ times $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, with $F_a$ its component along $x_a$. Integrating the conservation law
$\partial_t q + \nabla\cdot\mathbf F = 0$ over cell $i$ and applying the divergence theorem gives, line by line,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_{V_i}\partial_t q\,\mathrm{d}V + \oint_{\partial V_i}\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf n\,\mathrm{d}A &= 0, \\
V_i\,\frac{\mathrm{d}\overline q_i}{\mathrm{d}t}
 + \sum_{a=1}^{3}\left(A_{a,+}\overline F_{a,+} - A_{a,-}\overline F_{a,-}\right) &= 0, \\
\frac{\mathrm{d}\overline q_i}{\mathrm{d}t}
 &= -\frac{1}{V_i}\sum_{a=1}^{3}\left(A_{a,+}\overline F_{a,+} - A_{a,-}\overline F_{a,-}\right),
\end{aligned}
$$

with $\overline q_i$ the cell average, $A_{a,\pm}$ the areas of the two faces normal to $x_a$ from
@eq-ch03-cartesian-metric and $\overline F_{a,\pm}$ the face-average fluxes through them. The second line holds because
each face is flat with a constant outward normal $\pm\hat{\mathbf e}_a$. No further term appears: the basis vectors
are constant, so a vector field's components obey the same law as a scalar's. The last line is
`CoordinateImpl::divergence` followed by $\Delta\overline q_i = -\Delta t$ times it
({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::divergence >}}, {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}). Every quantity here is exact: the check integrates the three face
measures and $\mathrm{d}V$ over the cell in sympy and recovers $A_{i\pm1/2} = \Delta x_2\Delta x_3$,
$A_{j\pm1/2} = \Delta x_1\Delta x_3$, $A_{k\pm1/2} = \Delta x_1\Delta x_2$ and $V_i$[^rg-10e86c4afb2b], and the uniform-weight
centroid as the midpoint, each with zero residual (`[C17]`).[^cart-c17] The Tests layer adds the product test on
the built grid.

[^cart-c17]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.out`,
    line `[C17]`; a sympy restatement of `CoordinateImpl::face_area1` to `face_area3`, `CoordinateImpl::cell_volume`
    and `CartesianImpl::reset` at the pin, CPU, double; Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0.

### Numerical method

Widths `dx1f`, `dx2f`, `dx3f` are cell quantities, one per cell including ghosts; `x1v` holds the midpoints; `dx1v`
(the centre spacing) equals the width. All are built once in `reset` from the global width, except on a stretched
$x_1$: there `x1_metrics_` takes `dx1f` as the face differences, `x1v` as the face midpoints and `dx1v` as the
midpoint differences of the global faces with their mirrored ghosts
({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::x1_metrics_ >}}). The divergence takes the
face fluxes $\mathbf F_a$[^rg-e63dc7183ace] (face averages, from the Riemann solver), multiplies them by the face areas, differences
them across each interior cell and divides by $V_i$; ghost cells receive no divergence. @fig-ch03-cartesian-cell
draws one cell with its three face areas.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-cartesian-cell
#| fig-cap: "One Cartesian cell with its widths and the three face areas $\\Delta x_2\\Delta x_3$, $\\Delta x_1\\Delta x_3$ and $\\Delta x_1\\Delta x_2$; the centre is the midpoint. Widths are in m, areas in $\\mathrm{m}^2$."
#| fig-alt: "A box with its three widths labelled and one face of each orientation shaded."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch03.figures.fig_cartesian_cell import make_fig
make_fig()
```

A mesh generator (`reset_coordinates`) may move the faces; the Cartesian override then recomputes widths, midpoints
and centre spacings from the moved faces, so the grid need not be uniform and @eq-ch03-cartesian-metric uses the
local widths ({{< code src/coord/cartesian.cpp CartesianImpl::reset_coordinates >}} for the $x_1$ part).

A stretched $x_1$ grid (for example, one refined near the surface) is requested in the deck, with
`geometry/x1f` (a face list) or `geometry/cells/x1rat` (a geometric ratio); @sec-ch03-globalgrid derives the faces
and lists what such a deck must satisfy. No YAML key and no Python binding reaches `reset_coordinates`.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| widths, centres, zero cosine | {{< code src/coord/cartesian.cpp CartesianImpl::reset >}} | `reset` | `type: cartesian` |
| $x_1$ widths and centres | {{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::x1_metrics_ >}} | `x1_metrics_` | `geometry/x1f`, `geometry/cells/x1rat` |
| face areas and volume | {{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::cell_volume >}} | `cell_volume` | none |
| flux divergence | {{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::divergence >}} | `divergence` | none |
| stage operator (no source) | {{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::forward >}} | `forward` | none |
| type selection | {{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::create >}} | `create` | `geometry.type` |

: Code map of the Cartesian metric. {#tbl-ch03-cartesian-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-cartesian-code):

1. `create` builds a `Cartesian` module when `type` is `cartesian`; an unknown type stops setup with "Unknown
   coordinate type" ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::create >}}).
2. `reset` sets the three cosine buffers to zero, the $x_1$ widths, midpoints and centre spacings from
   `x1_metrics_` (the global width on a uniform $x_1$, the faces on a stretched one), and those of $x_2$, $x_3$ from
   the global width ({{< code src/coord/cartesian.cpp CartesianImpl::reset >}}).
3. In each stage, `forward` returns the `divergence` of the three fluxes and ignores the face pressure
   ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::forward >}}); `divergence` forms the area-weighted differences over the interior cells
   and divides by `cell_volume` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::divergence >}}).

**How to use it.** Cartesian is the type when `geometry.type` is absent or `cartesian`; the grid keys are those of
@sec-ch03-globalgrid:

```yaml
geometry:
  type: cartesian
  bounds: {x1min: 0., x1max: 1000., x2min: 0., x2max: 1000.}
  cells: {nx1: 8, nx2: 8, nghost: 2}
```

Refused: any other type name stops setup in `create` with "Unknown coordinate type: <name>". The type selection is
({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::create >}}):

```cpp
  if (opts->type() == "cartesian") {
    return p->register_module(name, Cartesian(opts, p));
  } else if (opts->type() == "cylindrical") {
    return p->register_module(name, Cylindrical(opts, p));
  } else if (opts->type() == "spherical-polar") {
    return p->register_module(name, SphericalPolar(opts, p));
  } else if (opts->type() == "gnomonic-equiangle") {
    return p->register_module(name, GnomonicEquiangle(opts, p));
  } else {
    TORCH_CHECK(false, "Unknown coordinate type: ", opts->type());
  }
```

`cylindrical` is accepted here but builds no metric (@sec-ch03-cylindrical).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_coordinate` | the volume is the product of the caller's widths | $10^{-14}$ relative | round-off of a three-factor product |
| `test_coordinate` | a degenerate $x_1$ beside live axes has width 5 | $10^{-14}$ absolute | round-off of one difference |

: Tests of the Cartesian metric. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-cartesian-tests}

The cases are `cell_volume_is_the_product_of_the_callers_widths` ({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp CoordinateProgrammatic.cell_volume_is_the_product_of_the_callers_widths >}}) and
`a_degenerate_axis_beside_live_ones` ({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp CoordinateProgrammatic.a_degenerate_axis_beside_live_ones >}}). Both run on CPU only, one block, one
rank. They were not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).

### Limits

No known limits beyond those of the global grid (@sec-ch03-globalgrid). The divergence of a mesh-generator grid is not
tested at the pin (not measured). The switch combinations that are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
